column1: # spec-coverage-scope-baseline.tsv — the frozen R-03 proof (ADR-0138 §D5, issue #312, Task 6).
# WHAT THIS IS. One row per (SPEC, declared id) pair in the completed (spec, plan) corpus, each
# carrying the SCOPED verdict spec-coverage.sh produces today: COVERED or UNSCOPED. This is a
# per-item FROZEN baseline, not a floor — CLAUDE.md rule 10 / ADR-0124: a >= N assertion over a
# population with slack still passes when its own plant removes one member; an exact per-row
# comparison is what a plant actually bites.
# HOW IT IS PRODUCED, EXACTLY (do not hand-edit a row without re-running this). The population is
# derived by issue-number prefix: for each docs/specs/<N>-*.spec.md that declares at least one
# R-NN id (spec_declares_ids()), find docs/superpowers/plans/<date>-<N>-*.md, falling back to
# docs/superpowers/plans/<date>-<slug>.md when the plan filename carries no bare issue number (the
# corpus has both forms). NEVER paired through a manifest — most manifests' artifacts.spec still
# points at the mutable root SPEC.md slot, which silently reduces to N copies of whichever feature
# is in flight. The chain currently producing THIS file is itself excluded from the population: an
# in-flight chain is not a completed corpus member. For every resolved (spec, plan) pair, every
# declared id's verdict is read straight off `spec-coverage.sh --spec <spec> --plan <plan>
# --tests-root <repo-root>`'s own stdout — COVERED / UNSCOPED / UNCOVERED — never re-interpreted.
# The exact derivation lives in staging/plugin/scripts/tests/spec-coverage.test.sh, section RS7-RS8
# (RS_PAIRS / RS_LIVE) — that shell IS the regeneration procedure; this file's rows must equal its
# output byte-for-byte or RS7/RS8a/RS8b fail on the specific diverging row.
# WHEN TO REGENERATE. Whenever a concept-to-code chain completes and its SPEC+plan pair becomes the
# 16th (or Nth) member of the corpus above, RS8b goes RED on that new pair's rows (a live verdict
# with no baseline counterpart). Re-run the RS7/RS8 derivation block against the current repo state,
# diff the result against this file, and append/update rows for the new pair only — never rewrite a
# row for a SPEC whose chain was already complete and frozen here (CLAUDE.md rule 14: a historical
# record is corrected forward, not in place). A row can also change if a later feature adds or
# renames a test file that shifts an existing pair's scope; that is a real drift signal and RS7
# reporting it red is the mechanism working, not a false alarm to silence by re-freezing blindly.
# MEASURED 2026-08-14 (re-derive, do not trust this comment per CLAUDE.md rule 13): 15 (spec, plan)
# pairs, 117 declared ids, 93 COVERED, 24 UNSCOPED (20 classed testable, 4 classed
# not-test-assertable). RS9a/RS9b assert only a >= 15 / >= 100 vacuity floor on the DERIVATION
# (rule 10) — this file's 117 exact rows, compared row-by-row in RS7/RS8, are where R-03 is actually
# 2026-08-18 — REGENERATED UNDER ADR-0154 (Task 5, spec-coverage-scope-back-reference). The scope
# filter became a conjunction — a discovered test file must ALSO name the feature back, not only
# be named by the plan — see spec-coverage.sh's own header and ADR-0154 §D1/§D5. STARTING STATE,
# re-derived the same day rather than trusted from the 2026-08-14 sentence above (CLAUDE.md rule
# 13): 16 (spec, plan) pairs, 130 declared ids, 106 COVERED, 24 UNSCOPED. The corpus had already
# grown by one completed pair since 2026-08-14, for reasons unrelated to this feature and not
# investigated further here — out of this task's scope.
# The RS7/RS8 derivation (spec-coverage.test.sh, section RS7-RS10, which IS the regeneration
# procedure — no row below was hand-edited) was re-run against this same 16-pair corpus with
# ADR-0154's conjunction filter already in place (commit 2102eeb) and diffed, row by row, against
# every row already committed here. RESULT: ZERO verdict changes and ZERO row-count changes — the
# regenerated (spec, id, verdict) set is byte-identical to what was already committed. PER-ROW
# ACCOUNTING: none required (0 of 130 rows differ; no COVERED -> UNSCOPED flip, no UNSCOPED ->
# COVERED flip). This confirms ADR-0154's M4 prediction on this feature's own corpus: the
# back-reference conjunction narrows the wider 52-plan/263-file scope population (94 files dropped,
# per the ADR) without moving a single frozen verdict in the narrower (spec, id) corpus this file
# NO ARCHIVED SPEC IS EDITED FOR THIS FILE (CLAUDE.md rule 14, ADR-0138 §D5). Retro-fitting
# `(no-test: ...)` into the 4 completed SPECs behind the not-test-assertable rows below would
# correct a historical record in place. This file is a new record ABOUT that corpus, written
# forward; `no-test:` (ADR-0138 §D4) governs SPECs written from now on, this baseline governs the
#   testable            — genuine drift: the gate was silently passing this id via a foreign or
#                          unlisted test-file mention before scoping landed.
#   not-test-assertable — a documentation, process, or external-process obligation with nothing
#                          executable to assert; the residual false-negative class ADR-0138 §D4
#                          exists to exempt going forward via (no-test: ...).
# A line beginning with "#" in column 1 is a comment; spec-coverage.test.sh's RS8b skips it
# explicitly (`case "$_bn" in \#*) continue ;; esac`) and neither RS7 nor RS8a reads this file's
# lines directly (they iterate the LIVE side and probe the baseline only for a specific (bn, id)
# pair), so a comment line cannot be mistaken for a stray (bn, id) row on either check.
